fields.h1: Build a Flashcard Quiz Maker That Tracks Every Missed Card
fields.hero_description: Build a flashcard quiz maker that turns your term list into cards and a quiz, and saves each answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Flashcard Quiz Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the deck, the quiz, and the table behind both. A follow-up prompt adds cards or changes the scoring.
fields.feature_1:
Cards and quiz questions from one list

Paste terms and definitions, one pair per line, and Emergent builds the card deck. The same pairs become multiple choice, typed-answer, or timed questions with no retyping.
fields.feature_2:
Wrong options drawn from your own deck

Each multiple choice question pulls its 3 wrong options from other definitions in the deck. A learner has to know the term, not spot the one answer that looks out of place.
fields.feature_3:
Every flip and answer saved as a row

Each card flip, answer, and time taken is a row in a database you own, tagged with the learner and the deck. Sort the table by misses to see which cards to teach again.
fields.feature_4:
Review dates set by each learner's misses

The app schedules each card per learner. A missed card comes back sooner and a known card waits longer. You set the gaps in days in your prompt and change them later.
fields.feature_5:
A pass mark that emails or posts in Slack

Set a passing score, such as 20 of 24, and the app emails a manager or posts in Slack when a learner reaches it. Anyone below the mark gets a new round of the cards they missed.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, your next deck

Host the decks on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository for next term.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Flashcard Quiz on Emergent?

fields.tab_content_1:
Cards that 8 or more students missed open Monday

Corrinvale High School's Spanish 2 class of 26 flips a 30-verb deck all week, then takes a 10-question multiple choice check on Friday. Any card missed by 8 or more students opens Monday's warm-up. This week that meant pedir, missed by 11, and seguir, missed by 9.
fields.tab_content_2:
Miss a word and it returns tomorrow

Ellery Kade studies a 200-word Italian deck on a phone each morning. A missed card comes back the next day. A card answered right waits 3 days, then 7 after a second right answer. Today's queue holds 34 cards: 12 missed yesterday and 22 coming due.
fields.tab_content_3:
A barista who scores 20 of 24 passes training

New baristas at Halsey Pike Coffee get 24 drink cards and type each recipe from the drink name. A score of 20 or more passes, and the shift lead gets an email with the barista's name and score. Of 14 new hires this month, 9 passed on the first try.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any answer over 5 seconds returns the next evening

Every evening, Lio practices 24 times-table cards for the 7s and 8s on a tablet at home. An answer that takes longer than 5 seconds goes back on top of the next evening's stack, even when it is right. Last night 7 x 8 took 9 seconds, and it leads tonight's 6 slow cards.

results.title: A Multiple Choice Check
results.description: Your answers lean toward a class deck where similar terms get mixed up. Build cards that flip all week and a multiple choice check whose wrong options come from the same deck, with a table of the cards the group missed.

results.title: A Typed-Answer Test
results.description: Your answers lean toward exact recall for a job, where a missing detail matters. Build a deck where each learner types the answer, with a passing score that emails a manager when someone reaches it.

results.title: A Spaced Review Deck
results.description: Your answers lean toward a long deck studied a few minutes a day. Build a deck that brings a missed card back the next day and spaces out the cards you know, with a short queue waiting each morning.

results.title: A Timed Speed Round
results.description: Your answers lean toward facts that need to come fast. Build short timed rounds that record how long each answer takes and put the slow cards on top of the next session's stack.

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a flashcard quiz maker a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 are AI generators that turn notes or PDFs into cards (Quizlet, Knowt, Quizgecko, Adobe) plus a Reddit thread asking how to turn a tab-separated term list into a multiple choice quiz. This page answers that thread: paste the term list, and Emergent builds one app that flips the cards, quizzes the same terms as multiple choice, typed answers or timed rounds, saves every attempt to a database you own, and shows which cards to review again. A matching quiz on the page names the format that fits the visitor's deck.
